thesis_summary.thesis: CoStar Group, Inc. (CSGP) is the dominant U.S. commercial real estate (CRE) data and marketplace platform. **[Fact]** Brokers and owners pay subscriptions for CoStar Suite research and analytics; LoopNet and related marketplaces monetize listing liquidity and advertising. **[Fact]** FY2025 revenue was **$3.25B** at roughly **79%** gross margin; **~89%** of revenue came from contracts of one year or longer. **[Fact]** The company is funding an expensive residential push (Homes.com) and absorbed Matterport (Feb 2025) and Domain (Aug 2025), which depress GAAP earnings while adj. EBITDA remains positive (**$480M** FY2025, **$161M** Q1 2026).
thesis_summary.why_market_wrong: A **transitory problem** may dominate: GAAP net income trough (**$7M** FY2025) and Homes.com marketing spend scare generalists away from a sticky CRE subscription core. **[Inference]** The stock is down roughly **54%** over twelve months to **~$33**, while CRE switching costs and data depth remain intact. There is no dated catalyst; residential share gain is optional upside, not required for base CRE economics.

key_assumptions.input: Starting free cash flow per share
key_assumptions.source: Normalized owner FCF: FY2025 adj. EBITDA $480M less ~$80M maintenance capex ÷ ~421M shares; GAAP FCF distorted by Homes.com/Matterport
CRE subscription mid-single-digit + marketplace recovery; marketing spend normalizes

open_questions: Confirm live price (~$33) and adj. EBITDA guidance
Subscription-only revenue bridge FY2023 to FY2025 for cleaner model
Homes.com unit economics (traffic, CAC) when disclosed
